claims.claim_text: The agronomist and educator Basil Mitrophanovich Bensin is a plausible but unconfirmed identity candidate for Basil M. Bensin at grade P-3 in the OSS index.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Basil Mitrophanovich Bensin, retired agronomist and educator
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional notice supplies the same uncommon full name and a professional career compatible with the index's P-3 context, but no direct OSS link.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable but unconfirmed. The uncommon exact forename, middle initial, and surname agree, and the professional career is compatible with P-3; no service number, personnel-file link, or OSS reference has been found.
claims.temporal_assessment: The institutional sources document earlier career affiliations but do not establish which, if any, immediately preceded OSS service.
claims.match_notes: No university, experiment station, seminary, publisher, or self-employment relationship is assigned as an immediate or last civilian pre-OSS affiliation. Box 50 must confirm the identity and chronology.

claims.claim_text: The official Army-entry record is confirmed as the Sergeant Nathan L. Benson listed in the OSS personnel index.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official files share the exact full name and exact private identifier; the Army-entry Private grade is compatible with the later Sergeant index grade.
claims.identity_match_assessment: A unique private identifier is decisive. Exact full-name agreement and compatible enlisted grades independently corroborate the match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record dates entry to March 4, 1941; it does not establish the later Army-to-OSS route or date.
claims.match_notes: The identifier is retained privately and masked publicly. Common-name candidates without it were rejected.

claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private identifier confirms that the coded Army-entry record belongs to the indexed Nathan L. Benson.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to Army entry, but not proven to identify a named employer, workplace, exact title, or immediate pre-OSS role.
claims.match_notes: No company, bank, office, agency, workplace, duties, or self-employment status is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The Peter J. Benson listed as GM 1/c in the OSS index is a high-confidence match to the Navy GM1 recorded by the Department of Veterans Affairs.
claims.evidence_excerpt: BENSON, PETER J / GM1 US NAVY
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official records agree on the exact full name and middle initial, Navy branch, and exact GM1 rating; the VA birth year is compatible with wartime service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence. Beyond the exact full name, the independent official record matches both the Navy branch and the uncommon exact GM1 rating. No private identifier is exposed or required for the public assessment.
claims.temporal_assessment: The VA record confirms service context and vital dates but does not establish when he joined OSS or his pre-OSS employer or assignment.
claims.match_notes: A 1924 newspaper candidate actually named Peter C. Benson and was rejected. Box 50 should confirm the personnel-file linkage and pre-OSS chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index establishes Basil M. Bensin at professional grade P-3 in Box 50. University of Alaska Fairbanks identifies Basil Mitrophanovich Bensin as a Russian-born agronomist and educator, and St. Vladimir's Seminary includes Basil Bensin among former faculty. The uncommon exact name and professional context make him a plausible candidate, but neither institution supplies a direct OSS or personnel-file link.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 50 to determine whether the indexed P-3 employee is the agronomist and educator and, if so, establish the immediate pre-OSS affiliation. No reliable immediate pre-OSS employer or assignment has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.
